## Request
Assess rates, FX, hedging, inflation and credit-relevant environmental, social and transition exposures for TransDigm Group Incorporated as of 2024-09-30 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is a retrospective FY2024 assessment, with future hedge terms distinguished from protection effective at year-end and no assumed market prices or forecast curves.

## Findings

### Bottom line
TransDigm has Moderate macro sensitivity: fixed-rate notes and effective derivatives cushion debt service, but substantial residual floating debt, a near-term hedge step-down and limited contractual inflation recovery leave free cash flow exposed.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–18; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 175–177; calculation C03

The supported closing-position calculation leaves USD 5,789 million unhedged and gives USD 57.89 million of annualised additional cash interest for a 100 bp increase. This is a static, pre-tax sensitivity, not a forecast. The issuer separately reports approximately USD 30 million; its bridge to the instrument terms is not established, so a single reconciled forward sensitivity is withheld. Labour inflation is the highest-priority supported social credit channel because skilled production and mostly unrecoverable contractual cost increases can squeeze margins before shipments or pricing adjust.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C07; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 73; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 18; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 22

### Key findings

- **Current mitigation is substantive, not complete.** Gross floating principal is USD 9,189 million, of which USD 3,400 million has effective swap or cap protection. Residual exposure represents 23.27% of carrying debt. The mechanical rate shock would consume 3.08% of FY2024 FCF before taxes and cash-interest income offsets; this supports Moderate rather than Low sensitivity.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C08
- **The first protection cliff warrants action before refinancing becomes urgent.** On 2025-03-31, expiring swaps exceed the starting collar, reducing covered notional by USD 900 million. Protection also changes from fixed base rates to a band; refinancing or repricing of loan margins remains outside that protection.
Basis: calculation C11; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 175–176
- **Inflation recovery is commercial discretion, not a blanket contractual hedge.** Most contracts do not permit recovery of raw-material, tax or labour increases. FY2024 gross margin nevertheless improved to 58.8% from 58.3%, showing operating mitigation in that year, not guaranteed recovery when volume absorption weakens.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 18; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 46
- **FX is a bounded secondary risk, not an established natural hedge.** Management says a 10% exchange-rate change would not materially affect FY2024 net income. Disclosed forwards cover selected transactions, but their strikes and the currency-matched revenue, costs and cash needed to measure residual liquidity exposure are not established.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 178
- **Environmental liabilities merit monitoring rather than a presumption of a financing impairment.** Recorded remediation obligations total USD 41 million versus USD 44 million previously; payment timing and excess exposure are not sized. Product safety and physical disruption are contingent cash-loss channels, not evidence of an existing uninsured loss or a measurable refinancing penalty.
Basis: calculation C14; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 31; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 160–161

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view
The strongest counterargument is demonstrated mitigation: the issuer reports approximately 77% fixed-rate debt, the derivatives qualify as effective cash-flow hedges, gross margin improved despite inflation and FY2024 FCF was USD 1,880 million. Those facts argue against a rate-driven near-term liquidity crisis. They do not make forward-starting collars current protection or convert FX notional into a verified net exposure hedge. A reconciled cash-interest bridge, replacement protection before expiries and evidence that contract repricing keeps pace with wages would strengthen the case for lower sensitivity. Persistent cost growth with weaker shipments, unrenewed protection or production interruptions would move the assessment higher.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 73; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 176–178; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 46; Financial foundation (CP-1)

### Limitations

- The reported and term-based rate sensitivities do not share an explained reconciliation. Consequently, the closing-position calculation is suitable as a defined mechanical sensitivity, but neither result is adopted as a reconciled forward cash-interest forecast.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 73; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 176; calculation C10
- Swap disclosure illustrates all-in rates using an older loan margin, while the debt schedule shows subsequent repricing. This does not invalidate base-rate protection, but prevents using those illustrative all-in rates as current loan coupons or forecasting exact hedge savings by tranche.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 152–153; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 176
- The disclosed FX test concerns historical net income, not jurisdictional cash available for debt service. Without matched currency cash flows, forward strikes and covenant translation rules, no numerical natural-hedge ratio, residual FX cash shock or covenant-currency cushion is established.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 178
- Employee-cost amounts, contract repricing dates and facility-specific loss protection are not supplied. The labour and physical-risk assessment therefore identifies cash-flow channels and triggers, not a measured stressed cash loss or an incremental financing premium.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–18; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 22; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26

### Macro and hedging view
The largest identified unhedged rate position is the term-loan balance after effective derivatives, followed by the receivables facility. Caps protect increases above their strikes, not a permanently fixed coupon; collars also surrender benefit below their floors. None protects refinancing credit spreads. The Moderate assessment reflects limited immediate FCF sensitivity relative to historical cash generation, offset by the dated loss of protection and contract cost-recovery constraints. It does not imply a measured joint downside tolerance for rates, demand, wages and discretionary cash use.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C07; calculation C08; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–18; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 175–176; Fundamental credit (CP-2)

### Credit implication
Skilled-labour cost and production continuity are the highest-priority supported social factors for Fundamental credit and Committee decision. Wage pressure meets fixed-price commitments with limited recovery rights; vacancies or a work stoppage can then delay production while financing costs continue. The supported consequence is weaker operating cash generation and slower liquidity rebuilding, not an inferred default probability or recovery haircut. Environmental compliance was not materially burdensome in FY2024, and current disclosures do not establish an ESG-specific refinancing premium. At the next reporting update and before the first hedge transition, monitor wage pressure, contract repricing, delivery interruptions and protection replacement together. Governance and shareholder conduct remain the assessment of Business & governance rather than a duplicated ESG judgement.
Basis: TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–13; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 18; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 22; TDG_2024-09-30_10-K_0001260221-24-000083_tdg-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 176; Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Calculations

Calculations use consolidated USD million amounts at 2024-09-30 unless a row identifies a different period. Interest sensitivities are annualised static pre-tax cash-cost changes, not predictions of rates, balances, borrower default or cash-interest income. Positive additional interest is an outflow; the corresponding FCF change is negative. The cap is counted for an upward shock above its disclosed strike; future collars are excluded from current protection. Debt amortization, basis/reset mismatches, taxes, fees, counterparty failure and portfolio changes are not modelled.
